headline: Residential tax exemption set at 35%, $800,000 cut from Public Works budget, and new inclusionary zoning rules passed.
summary: The $800,000 cut from the Public Works budget will instead be raised on the FY 2027 tax recapitulation report. The 35% residential exemption was kept, and new inclusionary zoning rules passed. Papers on public shade trees, a National Grid easement at Forest Dale Cemetery, and $11,173,912.75 in free cash went to committee.
decisions: Referred the public shade trees paper to a joint meeting of the Public Properties and Rules and Ordinance committees.
Approved cutting $800,000 from the FY 2027 Public Works budget for the FY 2026 snow and ice deficit, 9-1.
Approved keeping the 35% residential exemption and setting a 0.9059 minimum residential factor for FY 2027 tax rates, 10-0.
Referred to Finance the transfer of $11,173,912.75 from free cash to two new stabilization funds.
Referred to the Public Properties committee the proposed National Grid easement at Forest Dale Cemetery.
Approved accepting a $420,000 state park grant for Linden Park Playground improvements.
Approved and ordained the revised inclusionary zoning ordinance, Code 12.12.300.
Approved and ordained a new subsection F, Incentives, to the inclusionary zoning code.
Approved and ordained moving supervision of the animal control officer from the police department to health and inspectional services.
discussion: Snow and ice deficit: Members asked why the $800,000 had to come out of the Public Works budget. Finance staff said state law lets cities run a snow and ice deficit and raise it the next year.
Residential exemption: Members asked how many residential taxpayers would pay less this year. The assessor said 8,100 people receive the exemption, at $3,361 per household.

Forest Dale Cemetery easement: Cemetery trustees said National Grid damaged trees and a leaning pole on Forest Street still needs fixing. Members debated whether a revocable license would work better than an easement.
Inclusionary zoning conflicts: Members said the rules need to match the MBTA zoning rules and the Overlook Ridge overlay. A meeting is set for December 1.
